meta.title: Beanscape — a world in every cup
meta.description: An independent encyclopedia of coffee: its history, its drinks, how it is grown, roasted and brewed, and what it means in kitchens around the world.

stage.inviteAction: Crack the coffee bean and begin
stage.headline: Every cup has a story.
stage.sub: Steam, crema and aroma are suggested here with light and motion. Your screen cannot carry the smell — the rest of the site carries the knowledge.
stage.fallbackTitle: Your browser is not running 3D graphics.
stage.fallbackBody: The opening sequence needs WebGL. Everything else on Beanscape works without it — carry on down to the contents.
stage.canvasLabel: An animated sequence: a coffee bean cracks open and becomes a cup of coffee.

statement.body1: Beanscape is a reference for people who drink coffee and want to understand it. Where it came from, why a cortado is not a flat white, what roasting actually changes, and how the same bean becomes six different drinks in six different countries.
statement.body2: Nothing here is for sale. It is a self-initiated project, written and built in the open.

contents.title: Contents
contents.note: Five sections. The opening sequence is finished; the rest are being written.

history.name: Coffee History
history.desc: From the Ethiopian highlands to Yemeni ports, Ottoman coffeehouses and the plantations that followed — with the legends kept separate from the record.

discover.name: Discover Coffee
discover.desc: A searchable directory of coffee drinks: espresso, cortado, Turkish coffee, Vietnamese egg coffee and many more, each with its origin and flavour profile.

recipes.name: Recipes & Brewing
recipes.desc: How to actually make them. Ratios, grind, water temperature, timings, equipment, and the mistakes that spoil a cup.

journey.name: From Bean to Cup
journey.desc: Cherry, seed, drying, roast, grind, extraction — what changes at each stage and why you can taste the difference.

world.name: Coffee Around the World
world.desc: Growing regions and drinking cultures, mapped: who grows what, who drinks it how, and what coffee means at the table.
